deck_description:
Welcome to my Fiend Berserker Kuriboh Edison Format deck! This build focuses on a hybrid "Control and Bait" strategy to constantly pressure the opponent while setting up a massive, unexpected OTK.

Core Strategy The main goal is to generate early pressure with aggressive Fiends and -Skill Drain, while setting up our ultimate win condition: the -Kuriboh OTK. By loading -Darkness Neosphere into the GY via -Foolish Burial or using its own summoning condition, we can activate -Berserker Crush to give a tiny -Winged Kuriboh a massive 4000 ATK. When paired with -Staunch Defender, we force the opponent to crash their entire attack position field into our invincible furball.

Key Interactions & Combos The Goblin Bait Engine: -Goblin Elite Attack Force acts as a massive 2200 ATK beatstick. When it attacks and shifts to 1500 defense, it looks like an easy target for the opponent to run over. But when they declare an attack on it, we use it as field fodder (alongside a Fiend in hand like -Kuriboh) to Special Summon -Darkness Neosphere straight from the hand, blocking the attack and dropping a 4000 ATK boss monster on the board. Skill Drain Synergy: With 2x -Skill Drain active, -Goblin Elite Attack Force ignores its negative effect and stays in attack mode as a permanent threat. Meanwhile, the effects of -Giant Germ, -Grave Squirmer, and our Kuribohs all resolve in the Graveyard or hand, completely bypassing our own floodgate while shutting down the opponent's plays.

Main Deck Control Running 2 copies of -Skill Drain in the main deck gives us a massive edge in Game 1. It acts as a continuous floodgate that totally cripples top Edison decks like Blackwings, Machina, and Lightsworn, while we just swing over them with high-ATK beatsticks and our massive boss monster.

The Fiendish Side Deck Tech While our Main Deck focuses on the Kuriboh OTK and Skill Drain beatdown, our Side Deck features incredible Fiend-based utility. We bring in 3x -Possessed Dark Soul as our ultimate tech card. Not only is it a Fiend for our Neosphere discard costs, but it tributes itself to permanently steal the opponent's Level 3 or lower monsters, catching them off-guard and totally shutting down -Dandylion tokens, -Ryko, Lightsworn Hunter, and -Treeborn Frog setups.

Anti-Combo & Anti-Meta Tech The Side Deck is specifically tailored to crush the format's toughest matchups. We run 3x -D.D. Crow for aggressive Graveyard control against Zombies and Vayu Turbo, while -Cyber Dragon allows us to fuse away Machina boards into -Chimeratech Fortress Dragon. Additionally, -Light-Imprisoning Mirror keeps Lightsworn firmly in check, and we can bring in -Royal Decree for Games 2 or 3 to pivot against heavy-trap and Burn decks by swapping out our own -Skill Drain.

Feel free to test it out and let me know your thoughts in the comments!

deck_excerpt: 🌙 “The Moon rises… and your end is near.”
deck_description:
This version of Lunalight is built exclusively with 3 copies of the Legendary Decks ARC-V.

Although Lunalight finished in 2nd place at the 2025 World Championship, the archetype also received new support in the Legendary Decks ARC-V, notably with Lunalight Scarlet Tiger.

This new card is extremely powerful: it not only allows us to extend our combos, but, more importantly, to continue them even after an opponent’s interruption. It therefore gives the deck particularly impressive resilience against disruption.

Tri-Brigade Fraktall, although it is not part of the Lunalight archetype, also fits very well into the strategy. When necessary, it can allow us to start our combos or continue them after an opponent’s interruption. Together with Lunalight Scarlet Tiger, these two engines provide the deck with additional resilience, allowing it to play through numerous interactions and still end on a particularly strong board despite the opponent’s attempts to disrupt us.

The Legendary Decks ARC-V also contain the entire Lunalight engine, allowing access to the archetype’s full strategy with only 3 copies of the product.

The deck’s main objective is to Fusion Summon Lunalight Liger Dancer, our true boss monster. Thanks to the new support, it is now possible to end the turn with up to 3 copies of Lunalight Liger Dancer on the field, along with S:P Little Knight, creating an extremely difficult board for the opponent to break.

Lunalight Liger Dancer has 3800 ATK and is unaffected by the effects of cards that are not “Lunalight” cards. It is therefore particularly difficult to deal with, both through card effects and by battle. Its effect that destroys Special Summoned monsters controlled by the opponent also has a soft once-per-turn restriction: each copy of Lunalight Liger Dancer can use this effect once per turn. Therefore, if several Lunalight Liger Dancers are present on the field, each of them can use its effect, allowing us to generate multiple destructions and making the board even more difficult to deal with.

Lunalight is a combo deck that makes extensive use of its cards’ effects when they end up in the Graveyard. Lunalight Kaleido Chick notably allows us to send cards from the Deck or Extra Deck to the Graveyard in order to prepare different effects and access new combo lines. Its effect also has a soft once-per-turn restriction, which allows us to take advantage of it multiple times during the same turn by Special Summoning it again or bringing it back to the field. This allows the deck to quickly fill the Graveyard and chain together its combos.

Most Lunalight cards have particularly interesting effects when they are sent to the Graveyard, allowing the deck to turn the resources used during its combos into new possibilities for further plays.

Lunalight Gold Leo is the deck’s main starter. On its own, it allows us to start a large number of combos and can lead to a board that is extremely difficult for the opponent to deal with.

The deck also offers a very large number of ways to start its combos, making truly dead hands extremely rare. This multitude of starters and extenders gives the deck particularly appreciated stability and consistency.

Since the Lunalight engine is already quite large and takes up a significant portion of the available deck space, we prioritize essential cards and cards that provide high value to complete the list, such as Fuwalos, in order to maintain maximum efficiency without overloading the deck.

The deck does, however, have a few weaknesses. In particular, it needs to add many cards to the hand during its combos, making it vulnerable to cards such as Droll & Lock Bird. Despite this, it is still possible to establish a decent board even under Droll & Lock Bird.

Cards that disrupt the Graveyard also represent a significant problem, since the Lunalight strategy relies heavily on using and recycling its resources from the Graveyard.

The decklist presented here is a genuinely competitive decklist. Even though some small staples are not available in the Legendary Decks ARC-V, this version can already achieve good results at local or regional tournaments. It is also an excellent foundation for learning the Lunalight strategy and improving your skills with the archetype. With a few modifications and the addition of certain key cards, it is possible to optimize the decklist further in order to obtain a fully competitive version capable of competing with the Meta.

Overall, Lunalight is an explosive combo deck, but also particularly resilient thanks to its new support. With its ability to play through interruptions and build an extremely difficult board to break, the archetype remains an excellent option for players who enjoy Fusion decks and combo strategies.

The decklist presented here is therefore both an excellent foundation for discovering and mastering Lunalight, while also being competitive enough to aim for good results at local or regional tournaments. With a few improvements, it can evolve into a truly Meta-competitive version.

deck_excerpt: A consistent Monarch deck for Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Spirit Caller (NDS).
deck_description:
Deck Description

Spirit Caller Monarch is a Tribute Control deck built specifically for Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Spirit Caller on Nintendo DS.

The deck focuses on the classic Monarch strategy: establish Tribute material, summon a Monarch, resolve its removal effect, and gradually take control of the duel through repeated Tribute Summons.

Rather than relying on a single Monarch or a complicated combo, this build uses several different Monarchs with different forms of disruption, supported by defensive monsters, Tribute-based removal, and a large Spell/Trap control package.

The goal is to survive the early game, establish Tribute material, and turn every successful Tribute Summon into immediate card advantage or board control.

Monarch Lineup

The deck runs four different Monarchs, each serving a different purpose.

2× Mobius the Frost Monarch

Mobius is the deck's primary answer to opposing Spell and Trap Cards.

When Tribute Summoned, Mobius can destroy up to two Spell/Trap Cards on the field. This makes it particularly useful against decks that rely heavily on Set cards.

Mobius is especially valuable before entering the Battle Phase because clearing cards such as defensive Traps can make attacks considerably safer.

A common sequence is:

Tribute Summon Mobius → destroy opposing backrow → attack.

2× Granmarg the Rock Monarch

Granmarg provides another form of backrow removal, but unlike Mobius, it specifically targets Set cards.

This makes Granmarg useful when the opponent is relying on face-down cards and you need to remove a specific threat.

The distinction between Mobius and Granmarg gives the deck additional flexibility:

  • Mobius can destroy up to two Spell/Trap Cards.
  • Granmarg can destroy a Set card.

Granmarg therefore acts as another way to punish defensive boards without depending entirely on Mobius.

2× Thestalos the Firestorm Monarch

Thestalos attacks the opponent's hand rather than their field.

When Tribute Summoned, Thestalos forces the opponent to discard a random card from their hand. If the discarded card is a monster, it also inflicts additional damage based on that monster's Level.

This gives the deck a way to gain advantage even when the opponent's field is relatively empty.

Thestalos is particularly useful when the opponent has accumulated several cards in hand or when removing a card from the hand is more valuable than destroying something on the field.

2× Raiza the Storm Monarch

Raiza provides the deck's most flexible form of single-card removal.

When Tribute Summoned, Raiza can place a card on the field on top of its owner's Deck.

Unlike destruction, this does not simply send the card to the Graveyard. It can effectively remove an immediate threat while also manipulating the opponent's next draw.

Raiza is especially useful against cards that are difficult or undesirable to destroy.

Tribute Engine

The central engine of the deck is based around Treeborn Frog, Soul Exchange, and the defensive low-Level monsters.

Treeborn Frog

Treeborn Frog is the most important recurring Tribute resource in the deck.

Once Treeborn Frog reaches the Graveyard, it can return to the field during the Standby Phase under the appropriate conditions. This allows it to repeatedly become Tribute material for the Monarchs.

This is particularly powerful because the deck does not need to continually spend another card just to produce Tribute material.

The basic game plan is:

Treeborn Frog → revive → Tribute Summon Monarch → resolve Monarch effect.

One important consideration is that Treeborn Frog requires you to control no Spell/Trap Cards when its revival effect activates and resolves. Therefore, you need to manage your backrow carefully when planning to use Treeborn Frog as your recurring Tribute engine.

Soul Exchange

The deck runs 2× Soul Exchange as another way to facilitate Tribute Summons.

Soul Exchange allows one of the opponent's monsters to become Tribute material for your Tribute Summon.

This is extremely useful when the opponent controls a monster that is difficult to remove through normal battle.

For example:

Opponent controls a powerful monster
→ Activate Soul Exchange
→ use that monster as Tribute material
→ Tribute Summon Raiza/Zaborg/etc.

The important trade-off is that you cannot conduct your Battle Phase during the turn you activate Soul Exchange. Therefore, Soul Exchange should generally be viewed as a removal + Tribute setup tool, rather than something to use when you need to attack immediately.

Brain Control

Brain Control provides another way to convert the opponent's monster into Tribute material.

Instead of destroying an opposing monster, you temporarily take control of it and can use it as Tribute material for a Monarch.

This creates a powerful interaction:

Take opponent's monster → Tribute it → summon Monarch → gain additional removal.

This is particularly effective when the opponent has a single strong monster that is difficult to defeat through combat.

Defensive Monsters

The deck uses several low-Level monsters to survive until its Tribute engine becomes active.

Marshmallon

Marshmallon provides defensive value because it cannot be destroyed by battle while face-up.

It can therefore stall stronger monsters while you wait to draw a Monarch or Tribute enabler.

Spirit Reaper

Spirit Reaper serves a similar defensive role.

Its inability to be destroyed by battle makes it useful as a temporary wall, while its direct-attack effect can also force the opponent to discard a card.

This gives Spirit Reaper both defensive and hand-disruption potential.

Penguin Soldier

Penguin Soldier provides additional tempo control.

Its effect can return monsters on the field to the hand, allowing it to remove threats without destroying them.

It can also help clear the field before a later Tribute Summon.

D.D. Assailant & D.D. Warrior Lady

These two provide battle-based removal.

Rather than relying entirely on Monarch effects, the deck can use them to remove opposing monsters through their banishing effects.

This is particularly useful against monsters that are difficult to destroy normally or monsters that have useful Graveyard effects.

Sangan

Sangan provides consistency by searching appropriate low-ATK monsters from the Deck when it is sent from the field to the Graveyard.

It can therefore help find defensive monsters or other small monsters needed to establish the next Tribute Summon.

Breaker the Magical Warrior

Breaker provides another source of Spell/Trap removal while also functioning as a normal attacker.

This gives the deck backrow interaction even when a Monarch is not available.

Morphing Jar

Morphing Jar acts as a hand reset and draw engine.

When its effect successfully resolves, both players discard their hands and draw new cards. This can be useful when the deck has accumulated an awkward hand or when the opponent is holding a large number of cards.

Because this is a high-impact effect, it should be used carefully rather than flipped automatically.

Spell Removal and Board Control

The deck contains a relatively heavy Spell/Trap removal package:

  • 2× Giant Trunade
  • Heavy Storm
  • Mystical Space Typhoon
  • Breaker the Magical Warrior
  • 2× Mobius
  • 2× Granmarg

This gives the deck many ways to deal with defensive boards.

Giant Trunade

Giant Trunade returns all Spell/Trap Cards on the field to their owners' hands.

Rather than permanently destroying the cards, Giant Trunade is primarily used to clear the field and create a safe window for your plays.

For example:

Giant Trunade → clear backrow → Tribute Summon Monarch → attack.

It can also be useful when you need to remove your own backrow temporarily to enable Treeborn Frog.

Heavy Storm

Heavy Storm provides a full Spell/Trap wipe.

It is particularly valuable when the opponent has accumulated several Set cards and you need to clear the field before committing to a major play.

Mystical Space Typhoon

MST provides precise one-for-one removal.

Unlike Giant Trunade and Heavy Storm, MST can be used to remove one specific problematic card without affecting your own backrow.

Nobleman of Crossout

Nobleman of Crossout gives the deck another way to deal with face-down monsters.

This is especially useful when the opponent relies on defensive flip monsters or when attacking a Set monster would otherwise be risky.

Book of Moon

Book of Moon is one of the most flexible cards in the deck.

It can:

  • turn an opposing monster face-down;
  • disrupt a monster's position;
  • interfere with an opponent's setup;
  • protect one of your monsters from certain situations;
  • help create favorable battle situations.

It is therefore useful both offensively and defensively.

Premature Burial

Premature Burial provides additional access to monsters from the Graveyard.

In a Tribute-based deck, reviving a monster can immediately create another Tribute opportunity.

It can also bring back a useful defensive monster or previously used monster when you need to rebuild your field.

Swords of Revealing Light

Swords of Revealing Light provides temporary protection against attacks and reveals face-down monsters.

Its primary purpose in this deck is to buy time.

Monarch decks do not always establish their Tribute engine immediately, so having a card that can temporarily stop the opponent's attacks gives you additional turns to draw into your Monarchs and Tribute resources.

Trap Lineup

The Trap lineup is heavily focused on surviving the opponent's attacks and controlling the field.

2× Dust Tornado

Dust Tornado gives the deck additional Spell/Trap removal while also providing the ability to Set a Spell/Trap from your hand afterward.

This complements the Monarch lineup by allowing the deck to control the opponent's backrow even before a Mobius or Granmarg becomes available.

2× Sakuretsu Armor

Sakuretsu Armor provides straightforward monster removal when the opponent attacks.

It helps protect your Life Points and allows the deck to survive against aggressive decks until it can establish a Monarch.

2× Trap Hole

Trap Hole provides another layer of monster removal by responding to an opponent's Normal Summon.

It is especially useful against powerful monsters that would otherwise establish immediate board pressure.

Mirror Force

Mirror Force is the deck's strongest mass battle-removal option.

If the opponent commits several monsters to an attack, Mirror Force can punish the entire attacking field.

This is especially valuable when the deck is behind on board presence.

Solemn Judgment

Solemn Judgment is the deck's flexible emergency answer.

It can be used to stop an important Summon, Spell, or Trap at the cost of Life Points.

Because of its Life Point cost, it should generally be saved for plays that would otherwise significantly threaten your position.

Jar of Greed

The deck runs 2× Jar of Greed to improve consistency.

Rather than using complicated draw engines, Jar of Greed simply provides an additional card when activated.

This helps the deck reach important cards such as:

  • Monarchs
  • Treeborn Frog
  • Soul Exchange
  • removal
  • defensive cards

It also helps maintain the 40-card deck size without sacrificing access to additional resources.

Overall Game Plan

The deck generally plays in three stages.

Early Game — Survive

Do not rush into Tribute Summons if the board is not ready.

Use:

  • Marshmallon
  • Spirit Reaper
  • D.D. Assailant
  • D.D. Warrior Lady
  • Penguin Soldier
  • Trap Hole
  • Sakuretsu Armor
  • Swords of Revealing Light

to prevent the opponent from gaining too much momentum.

At the same time, try to get Treeborn Frog into the Graveyard.

Mid Game — Establish Tribute Control

Once you have Tribute material available, begin using your Monarchs.

Choose the Monarch according to the situation:

Mobius → remove multiple Spell/Trap Cards
Granmarg → remove a Set card
Thestalos → disrupt the opponent's hand
Raiza → put an important card on top of the Deck

This is the point where the deck begins generating its main advantage.

Late Game — Maintain the Advantage

Once the opponent's resources have been reduced, continue using your Monarchs and defensive cards to keep control of the field.

The objective isn't necessarily to perform one huge OTK.

Instead, the deck wins by repeatedly doing:

Tribute → Monarch effect → remove/disrupt → attack → repeat

Eventually the opponent runs out of monsters, backrow, and cards in hand.

Key Interactions

Treeborn Frog + Monarchs

The most fundamental interaction:

Treeborn Frog → revive during Standby Phase → Tribute Summon Monarch

This gives the deck a renewable Tribute source.

Soul Exchange + Monarch

When the opponent has a problematic monster:

Soul Exchange → use opponent's monster as Tribute → summon the appropriate Monarch

This effectively combines removal with Tribute Summoning.

Brain Control + Monarch

Another way to turn the opponent's monster into Tribute material:

Brain Control → take monster → Tribute it → Monarch

This can generate significant tempo because the opponent loses their monster while you establish a 2400 ATK Monarch.

Backrow Removal + Monarch

The deck has multiple ways to clear defensive cards:

Giant Trunade
Heavy Storm
MST
Dust Tornado
Breaker
Mobius
Granmarg

This allows you to choose whether to remove backrow before or during your Tribute play depending on the situation.

Strengths

Flexible removal:
The four Monarchs cover monsters, Spell/Trap Cards, Set cards, and the opponent's hand.

Strong Tribute engine:
Treeborn Frog and Soul Exchange make Tribute Summoning much easier.

Good defensive capability:
Marshmallon, Spirit Reaper, Sakuretsu Armor, Trap Hole, Mirror Force, and Swords of Revealing Light provide several ways to survive.

Multiple forms of interaction:
The deck can attack the opponent's field, hand, or resources depending on the situation.

No single-card dependency:
Although Treeborn Frog is extremely valuable, the deck can still function using ordinary Tribute material and Soul Exchange.

Weaknesses

The main weakness is that this is still a Tribute-based deck.

Drawing several Monarchs without enough Tribute material can produce an awkward hand. The deck therefore needs to carefully balance aggression with resource management.

Another important weakness is Treeborn Frog's interaction with Spell/Trap Cards. Because Treeborn Frog needs the appropriate empty-backrow condition to revive, you should not blindly Set every Trap when you are planning to use Treeborn as your next Tribute.

Similarly, Soul Exchange prevents your Battle Phase, so it should be used when its removal/Tribute value is more important than attacking that turn.

Recommended Playstyle

This deck is best played as a patient control deck.

Don't try to summon a Monarch every time you have one available.

Instead, ask:

Which Monarch gives me the most advantage in the current situation?

If the opponent has several Set cards:

Mobius

If there is one particularly problematic Set card:

Granmarg

If their hand is large:

Thestalos

If there is a monster or other card that you don't want to destroy:

Raiza

The strength of this deck comes from making the right Tribute at the right time, rather than simply summoning the biggest monster available.

deck_excerpt: If all goes to plan the person across from you will have exactly zero fun :)
deck_description:
This is a variant on the pure Magician decklist I posted a while ago with the new MAMO cards. I was watching an MBT video and he talked about Kali Yuga being a worse Azathot because rank 7s are more clunky to deal with than rank 4s and that gave me a thought. I had a look through the rank 7 pool for generic dark monsters and found exactly one that fits the bill of being able to detach two materials on turn one without running (more) main deck garnets. Voloferniges, the Darkest Dragon Doomrider lets you detach two to pop a face up card and if he has a dragon as material its a quick effect (but we don't care about that). Ideally you want to pop a copy of Double Iris Magician in order to get the search off while also ideally triggering an Astrograph/Starfrost, Star Pendgraph, or both.

 

Once you have a Voloferniges without material you just need to set the Rank-Up-Magic from the deck with Rusty Bardiche who's pretty easy to make. I did play around with Silent Boots rather than Doomed Soleret as the PK garnet because you can then banish him to grab a Fog blade as a backup negate in case the Rank-Up-Magic gets negated but I decided that was a little win-more and the advantage of Doomed Soleret is that if you open him you can just special him out to search the Rank-Up-Magic and then use him as material for Beyond the Pendulum of Override Dragon. Previously when I was testing with Silent Boots you would need to extend into Ignister to spin back the boots and then send with Bardiche which sucked and was generally terrible.

 

The deck is generally still bricky because you need 2-3 engine cards minimum to make plays and a fair few combinations of engine cards just do absolutely nothing on their own (think DA, Star Pengraph, and Harm). The central game plan is to summon horoscope or an Astrograph in order to make a pre pend summon Beyond or Override so we're playing loads of ways to search that.

 

There are two copies of Odd-Eyes Vortex Dragon because if you end on Exceed the Pendulum you can revive a Starfrost Magician from your grave in your opponents main phase which can then fuse itself with the Vortex on field to make a second Vortex and trigger its bounce as well as dodging droplet or imperm if need be.

 

The extra deck is extremely tight, so much so that I side the Zeus cards to swap in for the Kali Yuga BS when you know that you're gonna go second. I'm not all too married to the other side deck cards, the new Odd-Eyes is just a fun OTK tool which has an almost broken search effect that they had to make bad by putting another stupid restriction on. Duster and LS are reporting for duty to help overcome my fear of floodgates and solemns. When you know you're going first Judgement is just fun and Dragon's Mind is just another three Solemns because you typically end on at least one, possibly multiple monsters with exactly 2500 original ATK.

 

The handtraps are just the good ones, Fuwalos because its the best Mulcharmy and we only really have the space for one of them, Ash to kill other peoples Mulcharmies, and Droll because its just a good high impact one that unlike Nibiru you can keep to use when going first. Mulcharmies (other than Meowls enjoy your one draw lmao) are super scary so the Ashes help but Called by and Triple Tac are there for backup, I was playing Crossout but it just feels bad because it doesn't even work against Purulia for us so its basically another called by but only for Fuwa, Ash, and Droll which is maybe worth playing but the amount of non-engine is really pushing Magicians about as far as they can manage while still actually doing something most of the time.

 

To the three people who actually read this somewhat silly late night ramble, please let me know if you have any questions or suggestions because I love this pet deck to bits and can't wait to get my grubby little mitts on the physical copies of Horoscope, Starfrost, and Unicorn Parallel.

deck_excerpt: The deck that keeps on skipping...
deck_description:
The main concept of the deck is simple, keep the game going until you have the card called Magical Merchant on the field. This card has a simple Flip ability, which is that when it is flipped face-up you reveal cards from the top of your deck until a Spell/Trap card, then place the rest of the cards in the GY. This card is simple in just text alone, because what do you do when you Mill your deck, you need to know have a way to win. Even before that, what happens if you don't draw Magical Merchant your opening hand... Simple, delay, control, and search. Many decks in Edison format have a simple way to keep being reliable, which means a skilled pilot must be present for the deck to run well, now I am not the most skilled, or even the best pilot for this deck, but I have fun using the deck to have more of a explosive, usaully definitive win. 

Break Down of the deck...

First the delay portion of the deck
Cards such as Battle Fader and Cyber Valley. These cards simply delay a battle phase, stop it, and then gain advantage, unfortunatly it can't be a bigger package, since for the deck you want to find the Merchant before the opponent develops a board to stop you. 

Second the Control portion of the deck. 
Cards such as, D.D. Crow, Ryko, and Cyber Dragon. Now these control the opponent by stripping them of recources, we want the opponent to waste their larger removal tools to stop the aggression and to allow the plan to go through. D.D. Crow, strips any deck that uses DAD, or any other graveyard tricks to not be able to use them or stop the reallocation of those recources. Ryko gets rid of Monsters in the way, and even acts as removal in a pinch, preventing damage to pilot as much as possible. It removes most things that also control this deck as well. Finally Cyber Dragon, this card simply just removes other monsters and attract removal, this deck would rather not have the Merchant removed, so having the opponent hit the Dragon is a must.

Finally the Search and Win Portion. 
Cards such as Machina Gearframe, Witch of the Black Rose, Scrap Recycler, and Super-Nimble Mega Hampster. All of this cards search either for another piece of the deck, so the control portion, or the win con itself. (Which is Machina Fortress, Gallis the Star Beast and Cyber Eltanin in addition to the merchant.) Machina Gearframe searches for the other parts of the Machina engine, so the Fortress or Force. Scrap Recyler can trade in used or milled copies of the Machina engine to generate more cards, and even on normal summon, dumps the Fortress to the GY for us, which if needed allows the deck to work without being entirly dependant on a good mill, or specific cards to be milled. The Witch of the Black Rose, allows for the deck to have a reliable way to keep drawing deeper, allowing the spells to the grave keeping deeper mills, or searching deeper for any part of the deck, granted this is not a direct search but it does allow for cards to go even on advantage. The Super-Nimble Mega Hampster serves two purposes, there are only a select few cards in the deck that depend on flipping, which is Ryko and the Merchant, so the opponent will most likely want to remove the monster and not attack blindly into face-down cards. The second purpose is to search and dig for Ryko, which allows for even more removal of cards that hurt the game plan of a mostly monster deck. 
The win con of the deck relies on many factors, which is why the deck has multiple ways to win and refresh the deck. The deck does have a glaring weakness, which is drawing the game too long after milling, and then dying due to drawing empty. So there are many ways to force keep cards returning to the deck, and keeping the pilot alive. One of the ways the pilot stays alive is there being two spell cards, so if one gets milled early, you can try again, and second, you are not as likely to mill the entire deck and die before the pilot gets a chance to win. The two spell cards used are Pot of Avarice, which given milling most of the deck not only allows a refil on reliable forms of damage, it also allows the deck to plan a win, the pilot must keep track of what cards are in the deck to ensure even after the win con is attempted, that they can continue with more follow-up. The way to win with Pot of Avarice is to keep filling the deck with high level monsters, only if however, the card Gallis the Star Beast is hand. Gallis allows for the Pilot to keep revealing and milling more high level monsters to burn the opponent out. If Gallis is not in hand and the Machina Fortress is milled, then the high level machine monsters can be shuffled back to ensure the Fortress can keep coming back and placing pressure. The best way to win though is Cyber Eltanin, which turns all the monsters milled, if there is enough, to a win. The Eltanin allows the board to be cleared of monsters and places extreme amounts of pressure to instanly close out a game, although it will be a target of Solemn Judgenments and Bottomless Trap Holes.


The Sideboard is last and it is the hardest to manage based on expierence in the meta and what decks the pilot is expected to face, most of the sideboard is removal and control tools, the deck will remove some of the win-con and search elements to focus on removal of issues. Cold Wave and Ultimate Offering allow the pilot to block out counter play and sometimes, allow for card advantage on opponents turns. Monsters such as Ancient Gear Soldier allow the pilot to force the game win and allow for the game to be shut out during the battle phase and stop the opponents delays.

In Conclusion...
There are some cards I did not mention and those, function similarly to others in the deck, which allows for different plays and more sideboarding efforts without causing the deck to have as many weak points. The deck is very weak to very early aggression, and will have terrible match ups into Frog Monarch along with heavy removal and control decks. Which does not mean an auto lose, but can cause issues if unprepared for the situation. The decks strengths can be early game control, into a near unavioble win. Once a wincon loop or attack is established the deck just takes over games.

Thank you to any pilots that have left public deck lists and spear headed this stratgy, including Federico Mercuri and TimPontes, both deck lists and my local games shapped this deck to what it is now.
